messages:
maria: quick follow-up on the RFC — we need to decide placement for fused dequant in attention paths: do we do it inside the kernel (C++/CUDA fused operator) or keep a thin runtime dequant + generic kernel?

jia: kernel-level fusion gives better memory locality and fewer kernel launches. landed perf prototype: p50 token latency ~18ms vs 23ms for runtime dequant + generic attn. but it's more invasive. :thinking_face:

noah: key downside I saw: kernel-level fusion couples quant format assumptions to the kernel ABI. if we want to support FP8/INT8/INT4 with switching at runtime, we need a compat layer or many kernels. maintenance cost + test surface grows.

samir: curious about KV cache layout impact. fused dequant can avoid an extra write/read of the cached keys (so less memory traffic) but then cached KV must store quantized form or expanded form depending on where fusion happens. tradeoff: store quantized -> smaller memory but more dequant during read; store dequant -> simpler kernels but higher mem footprint.

maria: agreed. my position: prefer kernel fusion for the hot path but with a fallback generic kernel that can run dequantized inputs. require an ABI versioning approach.

olivia: for INT4 nibble packing we have an extra complexity: alignment and stride. packing layout differs across GPUs (some prefer 128-bit loads). If kernel does unpack+dequant inline we can optimize loads; runtime dequant would do scalar unpacking then memcpy -> slow.

jia: prototype kernel signature I sketched: 
```
// fused q,k,v dequant + attn
void fused_attn_qkv_dequant(const void* q_quant, const void* k_quant, const void* v_quant,
                            float* out, const DequantParams* params, int seq_len, int heads);
```
It takes quantized buffers and params describing scale/zero_point/format. single kernel eliminates a memcpy stage.

samir: question: how do we express fallback when format unsupported (e.g., new FP8 meta format)? do we detect at routing and fallback to runtime-dequant path? or let kernel return an error code and runtime retries?

noah: safer to detect at routing and pick path before issuing work. we already have model->variant routing. add a kernel-compat query in the model manifest. avoids wasted kernel attempts.

maria: rollout plan idea: behind feature-flag per-customer. canary small % on Dedicated first. metrics to watch: p50/p95 token latency, GC/memory pressure, KV cache hit latency, and token-level perplexity/regression on our eval set (to ensure numerics unchanged).

olivia: also add a smoke test that runs mixed sequence lengths (1, 32, 512) and both left- and right-padding. earlier prototypes regressed on odd padding shapes because of vectorized loads.

jia: FYI perf log from my run: 
```
config: int8-fused-kernel v0.1.2 canary
seq=32 batch=8 heads=32
old(path): p50=23.4ms p95=48.2ms mem=5.2GB\nnew(fused): p50=17.9ms p95=37.1ms mem=4.3GB\nfallback path (runtime-dequant): p50=24.0ms p95=50.0ms mem=5.0GB
```
numbers are noisy but consistent across a few runs.

samir: nice. but note p95 improvement smaller — suggests tail still dominated by scheduling / cuda-syncs. we should instrument kernel occupancy and streaming behavior.

maria: testing harness: add unit tests for numerical closeness +-1e-3 for fp8->float conversions and fuzz tests that randomly pick scale/offset. Also add an eval job to ensure we don't regress generation quality (we already have this for quant rollout but expand to include fused path).

noah: one more operational concern: when kernel ABIs evolve, how do we do canary rollback? we should keep the model manifest mapping to kernel ABI and preserve old image that still supports older ABI for safe rollback.

olivia: agreed. suggest adding an "abi_compat_level" field in the runtime config so the scheduler only deploys compatible kernels to nodes assigned to a tenant.

maria: next steps: (1) jia to clean up kernel prototype into a formal patch; (2) samir/olivia to spec KV cache layout options and migration story; (3) noah to add routing/manifest change for kernel capability detection; (4) I'll write rollout checklist + SLO/metric dashboards.

jia: will do. posting PR later today.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: canary gating enabled for feature flag `fused_dequant_attn` at 5% Dedicated capacity. Monitor dashboards: /dashboards/quant-attn-canary

maria: thanks team. we'll reconvene after the PR & KV spec. :thumbsup:
